name: Off-Road Motorcycle
description: A two-wheeled motor vehicle with a straddle seat and handlebars that its manufacturer intends for natural terrain, such as an electric dirt bike, registered with the DNR and ridden under the all-terrain vehicle rules.

restrictions.rule: Two wheels, a seat designed to be straddled and handlebars, intended by the manufacturer for use on natural terrain; includes a highway-titled motorcycle with design features for natural terrain
No limit on motor power or speed

Registered annually with the DNR through the county recorder ($15 plus a writing fee), with the decal displayed and the certificate carried, to ride on public land, public ice or a designated riding trail; a nonresident needs a DNR user permit instead
Titled as an all-terrain vehicle unless it already has a title as a road vehicle
Exempt from the all-terrain vehicle education certificate that riders aged 12 to 17 otherwise need

A rider under 12 may ride on a designated riding area or trail, public land or public ice only under the direct supervision of a certified instructor during a course, or of a parent or guardian 18 or older with a driver's license and riding experience
Helmets are required for riders and passengers at DNR designated riding areas, including their parking and loading areas
Carries a passenger only if built for one, and at DNR riding areas only with a driver's license
Must have brakes, and a lit headlight and taillight from sunset to sunrise
Kept off roadways and highways except where Iowa Code §321.234A and §321I.10 let a registered all-terrain vehicle ride, such as unpaved secondary roads and roads a county or city designates
Kept out of parks, wildlife areas, preserves, refuges and streambeds except on designated riding areas and trails
